किती लीटर पाणी मावेल ?
questions.solution:
b) येथे, लांबी (𝑙)=4 मीटर, रुंदी (𝑏)=3 मीटर, उंची (ℎ)=1.5 मीटर
हौदात मावणारे पाणी = इष्टिकाचितीचे (हौदाचे) घनफळ =𝑙×𝑏×ℎ=4×3×1.5=18 घमी (1 घमी =1000 लीटर )\begin{matrix} = & \mathit{l} \times \mathit{b} \times \mathit{h} \\ = & 4 \times 3 \times 1.5 = 18\text{~घमी~} \\ & \mathit{\ }(1\text{~घमी~} = 1000\text{~लीटर~}) \end{matrix}
∴ हौदात मावणारे पाणी =18×1000=18000 लीटर
∴ पर्याय (2) हे अचूक उत्त होय.

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text:
एका इष्टिकाचिती आकाराच्या पत्र्याच्या पेटीची लांबी 120 सेमी, रुंदी 80 सेमी व उंची
150 सेमी आहे. त्या पेटीस बाहेरून व आतून रंग द्यायचा आहे. (पेटीचा वरील पृष्ठभाग उघडता
येऊ शकतो.) ₹
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>𝟏𝟕𝟓</mn></math>
प्रतिचौरस मीटरप्रमाणे पेटी रंगवण्यासाठी किती खर्च येईल ? (उदाहरण सोडवताना
पत्र्याच्या पेटीची जाडी विचारात घेतलेली नाही.)
questions.solution:
b) येथे, 𝑙=120 सेमी =120100 मी =1.2 मी, 𝑏=80 सेमी =0.8 मी, ℎ=150 सेमी =1.5 मी
पेटीच्या आतील भागाचे पृष्ठफळ = पेटीच्या बाहेरील भागाचे पृष्ठफळ
आतील भागाचे पृष्ठफळ =2(𝑙𝑏+𝑏ℎ+𝑙ℎ) =2(1.2×0.8+0.8×1.5+1.2×1.5)=2(0.96+1.20+1.8)=2×3.96\begin{matrix} & \mathit{\ } = 2(1.2 \times 0.8 + 0.8 \times 1.5 + 1.2 \times 1.5) \\ & \mathit{\ } = 2(0.96 + 1.20 + 1.8) \\ & \mathit{\ } = 2 \times 3.96 \end{matrix}
आतील भागाचे पृष्ठफळ =7.92 चौमी
∴ बाह्यभागाचे पृष्ठफळ =7.92 चौमी
रंग देण्याच्या एकूण भागाचे पृष्ठफळ = (पेटीच्या आतील भागाचे पृष्ठफळ + पेटीच्या बाहेरील भागाचे पृष्ठफळ ) =7.92+7.92=15.84 चौमी  पेटी रंगवण्यासाठीचा खर्च = प्रतिचौरस मीटरप्रमाणे दर × पृष्ठफळ =175×15.84=₹2772 ∴ पर्याय (2) हे अचूक उत्तर होय

दर प्रतिचौसेमी ₹ 0.30 आहे, तर या दराने पत्रा बाहेरून लावण्यासाठी किती खर्च येईल

=6×( बाजू )2=6×(70)2=6×4900=29400 चौसेमी 
 पत्र्याचा खर्च = पत्र्याचे क्षेत्रफळ × दर =29400×0.3=₹8820\begin{matrix} \text{~पत्र्याचाखर्च~} & \mathit{\ } = \text{~पत्याचे क्षेत्रफळ × दर~} \\ & \mathit{\ } = 29400 \times 0.3 = ₹8820 \end{matrix}
∴ पर्याय (3) हे अचूक उत्त होय.

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text:

तयार होतील?
questions.solution:
a) मूळ घनाचे घनफळ =( बाजू )3=(15)3
तयार होणाऱ्या एका घनाचे घनफळ =( बाजू )3=(0.6)3
तयार होणाऱ्या घनांची संख्या = मूळ घनाचे घनफळ  तयार होणाऱ्या एका घनाचे घनफळ  =(15)3(0.6)3=15×15×150.6×0.6×0.6\begin{matrix} & \mathit{\ } = \frac{(15)^{3}}{(0.6)^{3}} \\ & \mathit{\ } = \frac{15 \times 15 \times 15}{0.6 \times 0.6 \times 0.6} \end{matrix}
∴ घनांची संख्या =15625
∴ पर्याय (1) हे अचूक उत्तर होय.

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text:
एका जमिनीत 8 मी लांब, 5 मी रुंद व 1.5 मी खोल असा खड्डा खणून त्यातील माती 25
मी लांब व 16 मी रुंद आयताकार भूखंडावर समान पसरली, तर तयार होणाऱ्या मातीच्या
थराची जाडी किती?
questions.solution:
c) खड्डा खणताना काढलेल्या मातीचे घनफळ = खड्ड्याचे घनफळ
=𝑙×𝑏×ℎ=8×5×1.5\begin{matrix} & \mathit{\ } = \mathit{l} \times \mathit{b} \times \mathit{h} \\ & \mathit{\ } = 8 \times 5 \times 1.5 \end{matrix}
मातीच्या थराची लांबी (𝑙1)=25 मी, रुंदी (𝑏1)=16 मी, थराची जाडी (उंची) (ℎ1) मानू.
पसरलेल्या मातीच्या थराचे घनफळ = खड्डा खणताना काढलेल्या मातीचे घनफळ
𝑙1×𝑏1×ℎ1=8×5×1.5
25×16×ℎ1=8×5×1.5
ℎ1=8×5×1.525×16=0.15 मी
∴ पर्याय (3) हे अचूक उत्तर होय.

=22×3×21×hcm3

ℎ=6×721

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text:
सोबतच्या
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>𝑂</mi></math>
वर्तुळकेंद्र असलेल्या वर्तुळात जीवा
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>𝑃</mi><mi>𝑄</mi></mrow></math>
व जीवा
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mi>𝑅</mi><mi>𝑆</mi></mrow></math>
आहेत. जीवा
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐏</mi><mi>𝐐</mi></mrow><mo>≅</mo></mrow></math>
जीवा RS.
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>𝑚</mi></math>
(कंस PYQ)
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>295</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow></math>,
तर
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>𝑚</mi></math>
(कंस RYS)
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo></math>
किती?
questions.solution:
d) 𝑚 (कंस PYQ) =295∘
लघुकंस PXQ चे माप =360∘ - संगत विशालकंसाचे माप
=360∘−295∘ 𝑚( कंस PXQ )=65∘
जीवा PQ≅ जीवा RS
∴𝑚 (कंस RYS) =𝑚 (कंस PXQ) ... (एकाच वर्तुळातील एकरूप जीवांशी संबंधित लघुकंस)
𝑚 (कंस RYS) =65∘
∴ पर्याय (4) हे अचूक उत्तर होय.

<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>𝑚</mi></math>
(कंस AYD)
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>140</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow></math>,
तर
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>𝑚</mi></math>
(कंस BAD)
<math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo></math>
किती ?
questions.solution:
d) व्यास AB मुळे वर्तुळाचे दोन समान भागांत विभाजन होते.
∴𝑚 (कंस ADB ) =180∘..... (अर्धवर्तुळ कंसाचे माप 180∘ असते)
∴𝑚 (कंस AYD) =140∘ ∴𝑚 (कंस DB ) =180∘ - संगत वर्तुळकंसाचे माप
=180∘−140∘
𝑚( कंस DB )=40∘
विशालकंस BAD चे माप =360∘ - संगत लघुकंसाचे माप
𝑚( कंस BAD )=360∘−𝑚( कंस DB) =360∘−40∘ 𝑚 (कंस BAD) =320∘
∴ पर्याय (4) हे अचूक उत्तर होय.

questions.solution:
d) The rational numbers 8163 and 10899 are greater than 1 , because their denominators are smaller than the numerators.
3645 reduced is 45=0.8
918 reduced is 12=0.5
Hence, 918 is the last number in the descending order.

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: What will be the second last number, if the following numbers are arranged in the ascending order? −1110,−1716,−1211,−76.
questions.solution:
c) The numerator is more by 1 than the denominator. Hence if denominator is smaller then that number is bigger. The fraction with smaller denominator is the greatest. Reverse is the case for negative fractions.
Denominators: −10,−16,−11,−6.
Ascending order : −16<−11<−10<−6.
Hence ascending order of numbers : −1716<−1211<−1110<−76
Second last number is −1110.
∴ the correct answer is option (3) .

questions.text: In △𝑃𝑄𝑅, seg 𝑃𝑋 is median. Length of median is 12 cm and 𝐺 is centroid. What is the length of seg 𝑃𝐺 and seg GX respectively?
questions.solution:
b) Centroid divides the median in the ratio 2:1
∴𝑙(PG)𝑙(GX)=21
∴𝑙(PG)=2𝑙(GX) Let 𝑙(GX) be 𝑥, then 𝑙(PG)=2𝑥
𝑙(PG)+𝑙(GX)=𝑙(PX)
∴2𝑥+𝑥=12∴3𝑥=12∴𝑥=4∴𝑙(GX)=4,𝑙(PG)=2𝑥=2×4=8.
∴ the correct answer is option (2) .

questions.text: In the figure, PS is altitude of △PQR and 𝑚∠RPS=50∘.𝑚∠SRP= ?
questions.solution:
a) In the figure, PS is altitude on side QR .
∴𝑚∠PSR=90∘,𝑚∠RPS=50∘
In △PSR, 𝑚∠PSR+𝑚∠SRP+𝑚∠RPS=180∘
∴90∘+𝑚∠SRP+50∘=180∘
∴𝑚∠SRP+140∘=180∘
∴𝑚∠SRP=180∘−140∘∴𝑚∠SRP=40∘
∴ the correct answer is option (1).

questions.text: (3𝑎+2𝑏)3−(3𝑎−2𝑏)3= ?
questions.solution:
b) Use expansion formulae.
(𝑎+𝑏)3=𝑎3+3𝑎2𝑏+3𝑎𝑏2+𝑏3
(𝑎−𝑏)3=𝑎3+3𝑎2𝑏−3𝑎𝑏2−𝑏3
(3𝑎+2𝑏)3−(3𝑎−2𝑏)3=[(3𝑎)3+3(3𝑎)2×2𝑏+3×3𝑎×(2𝑏)2+(2𝑏)3]− [(3𝑎3+3(3𝑎)2(−2𝑏)+3(3𝑎)×(−2𝑏)2+(−2𝑏)3] =[27𝑎3+54𝑎2𝑏+36𝑎𝑏2+8𝑏3]−[27𝑎3−54𝑎2𝑏+36𝑎𝑏2−8𝑏3]
=108𝑎2𝑏+16𝑏3
∴(3𝑎+2𝑏)3−(3𝑎−2𝑏)3=108𝑎2𝑏+16𝑏3
∴ the correction answer is option (2) .

questions.text: (𝑥−1𝑥)=5, then 7(𝑥2+1𝑥2)= ?
questions.solution:
b) (𝑥−1𝑥)=5
(𝑥−1𝑥)2=52 ... (Squaring both the sides)
𝑥2−2+1𝑥2=25
𝑥2+1𝑥2=25+2 ... (Adding 2 to both the sides)
[𝑥2+1𝑥2]=27
7(𝑥2+1𝑥2)=7×27=189 ... (Multiplying both the sides by 7 )
∴7(𝑥2+1𝑥2)=189
∴ the correct answer is option (2).

questions.text: (2𝑥+3𝑦−5𝑧)2= ____ ?
questions.solution:
c) (2𝑥+3𝑦−5𝑧)2= ?
Use this formula.
(𝑎+𝑏−𝑐)2=𝑎2+𝑏2+𝑐2+2𝑎𝑏−2𝑏𝑐−2𝑎𝑐
Keep the values in formula. 𝑎=2𝑥,𝑏=3𝑦,𝑐=−5𝑧
(2𝑥+3𝑦−5𝑧)2=(2𝑥)2+(3𝑦)2+(−5𝑧)2+2(2𝑥)(3𝑦)+2(3𝑦)(−5𝑧)+2(2𝑥)(−5𝑧)
∴(2𝑥+3𝑦−5𝑧)2=4𝑥2+9𝑦2+25𝑧2+12𝑥𝑦−30𝑦𝑧−20𝑥𝑧
∴ the correct answer is option (3) .

questions.text: If 𝑥+𝑦=5 and 𝑥𝑦=9, then 𝑥2+5𝑥𝑦+𝑦2= ?
questions.solution:
a) 𝑥+𝑦=5,𝑥𝑦=9 (𝑥+𝑦)2=𝑥2+2𝑥+𝑦2∴(5)2=𝑥2+2𝑥𝑦+𝑦2∴𝑥2+2𝑥𝑦+𝑦2=25\begin{matrix} (\mathit{x} + \mathit{y})^{2} = \mathit{x}^{2} + 2\mathit{x} + \mathit{y}^{2} & \therefore(5)^{2} = \mathit{x}^{2} + 2\mathit{x}\mathit{y} + \mathit{y}^{2} \\ \therefore\mathit{x}^{2} + 2\mathit{x}\mathit{y} + \mathit{y}^{2} = 25 & \end{matrix} Given expression =𝑥2+5𝑥𝑦+𝑦2 =𝑥2+2𝑥𝑦+𝑦2+3𝑥𝑦 ... [Statement and given values] =25+3×9=25+27 ∴𝑥2+5𝑥𝑦+𝑦2=52
∴ the correct answer is option (1) .

questions.text: The average speed of a vehicle is 24 km/h and it covers certain distance in 12 hours. If the speed of the vehicle is increased three times, then find the time required to cover the same distance.
questions.solution:
c) Let the speed of the vehicle be 𝑠 and the time taken be 𝑡.
There is inverse variation in the speed and the time.
∴𝑠∝1𝑡
∴𝑠×𝑡=𝑘
i.e. 𝑘=𝑠×𝑡
Taking 𝑠=24 and 𝑡=12,𝑘=𝑠×𝑡=24×12=288
... (Constant of variation)
Speed is increased 3 times.
That means 𝑠=24×3=72 km/h.
∴𝑠×𝑡=𝑘
∴72×𝑡=288
∴𝑡=28872
∴𝑡=4 hours
4 hours will be required to cover the same distance. If the speed of the vehicle is increased three times, the time required to cover the same distance will be 4 hours.
∴ the correct answer is option (3).

questions.solution:
d) Opposite angles of parallelogram are congruent. Measures of opposite angles are (4𝑥−20)∘ and (100−𝑥)∘
∴(4𝑥−20)∘=(100−𝑥)∘
∴4𝑥+𝑥−20=100−𝑥+𝑥
∴5𝑥−20=100
∴5𝑥=100+20
∴5𝑥=120
∴𝑥=1205
∴𝑥=24
∴ the correct answer is option (4) .

questions.solution:
d) The measures of angles are in proportion 1:2:4:5. Let the measures be 𝑥,2𝑥,4𝑥 and 5𝑥.
Now, 𝑥+5𝑥=2𝑥+4𝑥.
∴ two adjacent angles are supplementary.
Hence one pair of opposite sides is parallel.
∴ it is a trapezium.
∴ the correct answer is option (4) .

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The measures of two angles are 75∘ and 107∘ respectively. The measures of two remaining angles are equal. What are the measures of those remaining angles?
questions.solution:
a) Let the measures of remaining equal angles be 𝑥.
The sum of the measures of 4 angles of a quadrilateral is 360∘.
∴75∘+107∘+𝑥∘+𝑥∘=360∘
∴182+2𝑥=360
∴2𝑥=360−182
∴2𝑥=178∴𝑥=89∘
∴ measures of equal angles is 89∘ each.
∴ the correct answer is option (1).

questions.text: In the figure, ▫PQRS is a parallelogram. Ray SM and ray RM are angle bisectors of ∠S and ∠R respectively. 𝑚∠P=120∘, then 𝑚∠SMR= ?
questions.solution:
b) Ray SM is the bisector of ∠S and ray RM is the bisector of ∠R. ∴𝑚∠MSR=12𝑚∠ S and 𝑚∠MRS=12𝑚∠R 𝑚∠ S+𝑚∠R=180∘ \begin{array}{r} \mathit{m}\angle\text{ }S + \mathit{m}\angle R = 180^{\circ}\#(1) \end{array} ... (Interior angles) ∴𝑚∠MSR+𝑚∠MRS=12×180∘ \begin{array}{r} \therefore\mathit{m}\angle MSR + \mathit{m}\angle MRS = \frac{1}{2} \times 180^{\circ}\#(2) \end{array} ... [From and (2)]
∴𝑚∠MSR+𝑚∠MRS=90∘.
∴𝑚∠SMR=90∘
... (Remaining angles of △ SMR.)
∴ the correct answer is option (2).

questions.solution:
b) Suppose decided price be ₹ 100 .
<math display=xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mtext mathvariant="normal"> M. P. </mtext></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>30</mn><mi>%</mi><mtext mathvariant="normal"> of </mtext><mn>100</mn><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mo>=</mo><mn>130</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mtext mathvariant="normal"> Discount </mtext></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>%</mi><mtext mathvariant="normal"> of </mtext><mn>130</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mo>=</mo><mi>₹</mi><mn>13</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mtext mathvariant="normal"> S.P. = M.P. </mtext></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mo>=</mo><mtext mathvariant="normal"> discount </mtext></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mo>=</mo><mn>130</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>117</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{matrix}
\text{~M. P.~} & = 100 + 30\%\text{~of~}100. \\
 & = 130 \\
\text{~Discount~} & = 10\%\text{~of~}130 \\
 & = ₹13 \\
\text{~S.P. = M.P.~} & = \text{~discount~} \\
 & = 130 - 13 = 117
\end{matrix}</annotation></math>
Decided price = 100, Selling price = 117

questions.solution:
b) Marked price ₹ 1800, Discount per cent =12%

selling price = Marked price - Discount =1800−1800×12100=₹(1800−216)=₹1584\begin{matrix} & \mathit{\ } = 1800 - 1800 \times \frac{12}{100} \\ & \mathit{\ } = ₹(1800 - 216) = ₹1584 \end{matrix} . selling price of the watch is ₹ 1584 .
[OR
Meaning of 12% Discount is when Marked price is ₹100, Discount is ₹ 12 .
If Marked price is ₹ 1800 , let the discount be ₹𝑥.
Ratio of Discount and Marked price is the same.
∴𝑥1800=12100∴𝑥=12×1800100∴𝑥=₹216
Selling price = Marked price - Discount =1800−216 Selling price =₹1584.]
∴ the correct answer is option (2) .

questions.text: The average weight of 35 students of 8 th standard is 44 kg . Considering the weight of 2 teachers, the average weight becomes 46 kg . What is the total weight of two teachers?
questions.solution:
b) Average weight of 35 students =44 kg.
∴ total weight of 35 students =35×44=1540 kg.
Average weight of two teachers and students =46 kg.
∴ total weight of two teachers and 35 students (i.e. 37 persons) =37×46=1702 kg.
∴ weight of two teachers =(1702−1540)kg=162 kg.
∴ the correct answer is option (2).

questions.text: 5 years before, the mean age of a brother and sister was 8 years. The mean age of the brother, sister and younger brother is 11 years today. What is the age of younger brother?
questions.solution:
b) 5 years before total age of brother and sister =2×8=16 years  Their total age today =16+10=26 years
Total age of all three today =3×11=33 years
∴ the age of younger brother today = Total age of all three - Total age of two =33−26=7 ∴ age of the younger brother is 7 years.
∴ the correct answer is option (2).

questions.text: Mean of 25 scores is 58 . If one score is omitted, the mean of remaining numbers is reduced by 1 . What is the omitted score?
questions.solution:
a) Mean of 25 scores is 58.
∴ total of 25 scores =25×58=1450
If one score is omitted, the mean is reduced by 1=58−1=57
∴ total of 24 score =24×57=1368
Omitted score = Total of 25 scores - Total of 24 scores. =1450−1368=82 ∴ omitted score is 82 .
∴ the correct answer is option (1).

questions.solution:
b) <math display= xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: 
center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false" form="postfix">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mn>8</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mn>23</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mn>23</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>46</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>46</mn><mn>23</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{matrix}
 & 4(2\mathit{x} - 3) + 5(3\mathit{x} - 4) = 14 \\
 & 8\mathit{x} - 12 + 15\mathit{x} - 20 = 14 \\
 & 23\mathit{x} = 14 + 12 + 20 \\
 & 23\mathit{x} = 46 \\
 & \mathit{x} = \frac{46}{23} = 2
\end{matrix}</annotation></math>

<math display= xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>−</mi><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>−</mi><mn>24</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑥</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>−</mi><mn>17</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{matrix}
 & 4\mathit{x} + 12 = 3\mathit{x} - 12 + 7 \\

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The ratio of weights of copper and zinc in alloy brass is 13:7. Find the weight of zinc in grams in brass utensil weighing 1.2 kg .
questions.solution:
a) The ratio of weight of copper and zinc in brass is 13:7.
Let the common multiple of weight be 𝑥.
Then the utensil weighing 1.2 kg will have 13𝑥 kg copper and 7𝑥 kg zinc.
From the given information, 13𝑥+7𝑥=1.2
∴20𝑥=1.2∴𝑥=1.220∴𝑥=0.06
∴ the weight of zinc in the utensil =7𝑥=7×0.06=0.42 kg
1 kg=1000 g.∴0.42×1000 g=420 g.
Weight of zinc in the utensil =420 g.
∴ the correct answer is option (1).

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: Today the age of Sonal's mother is 3 times the age of Sonal. After 10 years, age of Sonal's mother will be 2 times Sonal's age at that time. What is the age of Sonal's mother today?
questions.solution:
a) Suppose, today's age of Sonal is 𝑥 years.
∴ age of Sonal's mother is 3𝑥 years.
After 10 years, age of Sonal will be ( 𝑥+10 ) years
and the age of Sonal's mother will be ( 3𝑥+10 ) years.
From the given condition, 3𝑥+10=2(𝑥+10)
∴3𝑥+10=2𝑥+20∴𝑥=10 years.
∴ today's age of Sonal's mother =3𝑥=3×10=30 years.
∴ the correct answer is option (1).

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The width of the rectangle is less than the length by 3 m . Find width of the rectangle if the perimeter of the rectangle is 82 m .
questions.solution:
d) Let the width of the rectangle is 𝑥 m.
Then the length of rectangle will be (𝑥+3)m.
The perimeter of rectangle =2 (Length + Width)
∴82=2[𝑥+(𝑥+3)]
∴82=2[2𝑥+3]
∴82=4𝑥+6
∴4𝑥=76∴𝑥=19
Width of rectangle is 19 m
∴ the correct answer is option (4).

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The sum of two numbers is 132 . The ratio of these two numbers is 5:7. Find these two numbers.
questions.solution:
a) The sum of two numbers is 132. Let the first number be 𝑥.
Then the second number will be (132−𝑥).
Ratio of the two numbers is 5:7.
∴ from the given information 𝑥(132−𝑥)=57
∴7𝑥=5(132−𝑥) ... (Cross multiplication)
∴7𝑥=660−5𝑥.
∴7𝑥+5𝑥=660
∴12𝑥=660
∴𝑥=55
∴ second number =132−55=77∴ the numbers are 55 and 77 .
∴ the correct answer is option (1).

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The ratio of two natural numbers is 5:4. If 56 is subtracted from both the numbers, then ratio of these two numbers becomes 3:2. What is the total of these two numbers?
questions.solution:
d) Let common multiple of two numbers be 𝑥.
Then the numbers will be 5𝑥 and 4𝑥.
Subtract 56 from these two numbers.
5𝑥−56 and 4𝑥−56.
From the given condition, 5𝑥−564𝑥−56=32
∴2(5𝑥−56)=3(4𝑥−56) ... (Cross multiplication)
∴10𝑥−112=12𝑥−168
∴10𝑥−12𝑥=−168+112
∴−2𝑥=−56
∴−2𝑥−2=−56−2∴𝑥=28
∴ the first number =28×5=140
and the second number =28×4=112.
Total of two numbers =140+112=252.
∴ the correct answer is option (4) .

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The denominator of a fraction is greater than the numerator by 2 . Fraction 74 is obtained if 4 is added to the numerator and 1 is subtracted from the denominator. Find the fraction.
questions.solution:
c) Let the numerator of the fraction be 𝑥.
Then the denominator will be 𝑥+2.
∴ fraction will be 𝑥𝑥+2.
In this fraction, add 4 to the numerator and subtract 1 from the denominator.
𝑥+4𝑥+2−1=𝑥+4𝑥+1
From the given condition, 𝑥+4𝑥+1=74
∴4(𝑥+4)=7(𝑥+1) ... (Cross multiplication)
∴4𝑥+16=7𝑥+7
∴4𝑥−7𝑥=7−16
∴−3𝑥=−9
∴−3𝑥−3=−9−3
∴𝑥=3 The fraction =𝑥𝑥+2=𝑥3+2=35
∴ the correct answer is option (3) .

questions.text: Train running at the average speed of 75 km/h reaches the destination on scheduled time. If the train runs at the speed of 90 km/h, then it will reach the destination 2 hours before scheduled time. Find the distance covered by the train.

b) Let the distance covered by the train be 𝑥 km.
Time = Distance  Speed 
𝑥75−𝑥90=2
∴𝑥75−𝑥90=2∴90𝑥−75𝑥75×90=2
∴15𝑥=2×75×90
∴𝑥=2×75×9015𝑥=2×5×90∴𝑥=900 km.
∴ distance covered by the train =900 km
∴ the correct answer is option (2).

questions.text: How much principal will be compound interest of ₹ 1590 after 2 years at the rate of 12% p.c.p.a.
questions.solution:
c) Suppose principal =P
If A=P×(1+R100)N then compount interst =A−P
∴1590=P(1+12100)2−P
∴1590=P×112100×112100−P
∴1590=P(1122−100210000)
∴1590=P×((112−100)(112+100)10000)
∴1590×10000=P×12×212
∴1590×10000212×12=P∴P=6250∴ Principal =₹6250

9261=8000(1+5100)𝑁
∴92618000=(105100)N∴(2120)3=(2120)N∴N=3

questions.text: An amount after 4 years is ₹ 2800 and after one years ₹ 2200 of a certain principal amount by simple interest then what is the principal amount?
questions.solution:
d) By simple interest after four years principal + interest =₹2800
After one years principal + interest =₹2200
∴ Interest of 3 years = ₹ 2800 - ₹ 2200= ₹ 600
∴ Interest for one year =6003=₹200
For 1 years principal + interest =₹2200
∴ Principal +200=2200
∴ Principal =2200−200=₹2000

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The compound interest on Rs. 30000 at 7% p.a. for a certain period is Rs.4347. Then find the period.
questions.solution:
c) Here
<math display=xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30000</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>.</mi><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4347</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mtext mathvariant="normal"> p.c.p.a. </mtext></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mtext mathvariant="normal"> Amount </mtext><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>.</mi><mi>I</mi><mi>.</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4347</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>34347</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mtext mathvariant="normal"> Amount </mtext><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>R</mi><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msup></mtd></mtr></mtable></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mn>34347</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>30000</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi>N</mi></msup></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{matrix}
 & P = 30000,C.I = 4347 \\
 & R = 7\text{~p.c.p.a.~} \\
 & \text{~Amount~} = P + C.I. \\
 & \  = 30,000 + 4347 \\
 & \begin{matrix}
A = 34347 \\
\text{~Amount~} = P \times \left( 1 + \frac{R}{100} \right)^{N}
\end{matrix} \\
 & 34347 = 30000 \times \left( 1 + \frac{7}{100} \right)^{N}
\end{matrix}</annotation></math>
<math display=xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mfrac><mn>34347</mn><mn>30000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mn>107</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑁</mi></msup></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mfrac><mn>11449</mn><mn>10000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mn>107</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑁</mi></msup></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mn>107</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="true" form="prefix">(</mo><mfrac><mn>107</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="true" form="postfix">)</mo></mrow><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑁</mi></msup></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"></mtd><mtd columnalign="center" style="text-align: center"><mi mathvariant="italic">𝑁</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\begin{matrix}
 & \frac{34347}{30000} = \left( \frac{107}{100} \right)^{\mathit{N}} \\
 & \frac{11449}{10000} = \left( \frac{107}{100} \right)^{\mathit{N}} \\
 & \left( \frac{107}{100} \right)^{2} = \left( \frac{107}{100} \right)^{\mathit{N}} \\
 & \mathit{N} = 2
\end{matrix}</annotation></math>

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text:
What will be the compound interest on principal of ₹ 1,00,000 for 212 years at the rate of 10% ?
(2019)
questions.solution:
d) Principal (P)=₹1,00,000; Period (N)=212 years; Rate of interest p.c.p.a. =(R)=10% Compound interest = ?
Period is 212 years
∴ half yearly rate of interest =5%(212 years =2 years +12 years ) 𝐴=𝑃(1+𝑅100)𝑁 ∴A=100000(1+10100)212 =100000(1+10100)2×(1+5100)1…(212 years =2 years +12 years )=100000(100+10100)2×(100+5100)=100000(110100)2×(105100)=100000×110×110100×100×105100=11×110×105\begin{matrix} & \mathit{\ } = 100000\left( 1 + \frac{10}{100} \right)^{2} \times \left( 1 + \frac{5}{100} \right)^{1}\ \ldots\left( 2\frac{1}{2}\text{~years~} = 2\text{~years~} + \frac{1}{2}\text{~years~} \right) \\ & \mathit{\ } = 100000\left( \frac{100 + 10}{100} \right)^{2} \times \left( \frac{100 + 5}{100} \right) \\ & \mathit{\ } = 100000\left( \frac{110}{100} \right)^{2} \times \left( \frac{105}{100} \right) \\ & \mathit{\ } = 100000 \times \frac{110 \times 110}{100 \times 100} \times \frac{105}{100} \\ & \mathit{\ } = 11 \times 110 \times 105 \end{matrix} ∴A=₹1,27,050  Compound interest = Amount − Principal =₹(127050−100000)=₹27,050.\begin{matrix} \text{~Compound interest~} & \mathit{\ } = \text{~Amount~} - \text{~Principal~} \\ & \mathit{\ } = ₹(127050 - 100000) = ₹27,050. \end{matrix} ∴ the correct answer is option (4).

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The population of a town increases at the rate of 5% per year. If the population of that town in 2012 was 1,20,000, then what will the population of that town be in 2015?
questions.solution:
a) The population in 2012(P)=1,20,000
Rate of increase (R)=5 p.c.p.a.; Period(N)=3 years;
After 3 years population (A)= ?
𝐴=𝑃(1+𝑅100)𝑁
∴𝐴=120000(1+5100)3 =120000(100+5100)3=120000(105100)3=120000×105×105×105100×100×100∴𝐴=12×105×21×214=3×104×441=138915\begin{matrix} = & 120000\left( \frac{100 + 5}{100} \right)^{3} \\ = & 120000\left( \frac{105}{100} \right)^{3} \\ = & \frac{120000 \times 105 \times 105 \times 105}{100 \times 100 \times 100} \\ \therefore\mathit{A} & \mathit{\ } = \frac{12 \times 105 \times 21 \times 21}{4} = 3 \times 104 \times 441 = 138915 \end{matrix} ∴ the population of the town in 2015 will be 1,38,915.
∴ the correct answer is option (1).

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text:
For a principal ₹ 10,000 the difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years is ₹ 81 . Find the rate of interest.
(2022)
questions.solution:
c) Principal (P)=₹10,000; Period (N)=2 years
Difference between compound interest and simple interest for 2 years =₹81.
Rate of Interest (R)= ?
Compound interest for 2 years =P(1+R100)N−P =10000(1+R100)2−10000=10000(100+R100)2−10000=10000(100+R)(100+R)100×100−10000=(100+R)2−10000=10000+200R+R2−10000\begin{matrix} & \mathit{\ } = 10000\left( 1 + \frac{R}{100} \right)^{2} - 10000 \\ & \mathit{\ } = 10000\left( \frac{100 + R}{100} \right)^{2} - 10000 \\ & \mathit{\ } = 10000\frac{(100 + R)(100 + R)}{100 \times 100} - 10000 \\ & \mathit{\ } = (100 + R)^{2} - 10000 \\ & \mathit{\ } = 10000 + 200R + R^{2} - 10000 \end{matrix} Compound interest for 2 years =200R+R2
Simple interest for 2 years =P×R×N100=10000×R×2100
Simple interest for 2 years =200R
As given compound interest of 2 years - simple interest of 2 years =81
200R+R2−200R=81
R2=81∴R=±9
Rate of interest cannot be negative. ∴R=9%
[Alternative method :
Let the rate of interest be R%.
The SI and CI for the first year will be the same.
∴ SI or CI for the first year =10000×R×I100=₹100R. SI for the second year =₹100 R.
CI for the second year =₹100R+ interest on ₹100R  Interest on ₹100R=100R×R×I100=R2 The difference in the compound interest and the simple interest is ₹R2.
This is given to be ₹81.
∴R2=81∴R=9%.]
∴ the correct answer is option (3).

a) Initial price of the car(P)=₹6,00,000;
Period ( N ) = 3 years;
Rate of depreciation (𝑅)=−10%
Today's price (A)= ? 𝐴=𝑃(1+𝑅100)𝑁=600000(1−10100)3=600000(100−10100)3=600000(90100)3=600000×90×90×90100×100×100=600×9×9×9=600×729𝐴=₹4,37,400\begin{matrix} \mathit{A} & \mathit{\ } = \mathit{P}\left( 1 + \frac{\mathit{R}}{100} \right)^{\mathit{N}} \\ & \mathit{\ } = 600000\left( 1 - \frac{10}{100} \right)^{3} \\ & \mathit{\ } = 600000\left( \frac{100 - 10}{100} \right)^{3} \\ & \mathit{\ } = 600000\left( \frac{90}{100} \right)^{3} \\ & \mathit{\ } = \frac{600000 \times 90 \times 90 \times 90}{100 \times 100 \times 100} \\ & \mathit{\ } = 600 \times 9 \times 9 \times 9 = 600 \times 729 \\ \mathit{A} & \mathit{\ } = ₹4,37,400 \end{matrix} Today's price of the car=₹4,37,400.
∴ the correct answer is option (1).

questions.text: From the given information, find the perimeter of pentagon 𝐴𝐵𝐶𝐷𝐸.
questions.solution:
b) △ABE,△EBC and △ECD, all three are right angled triangles. As per Pythagoras theorem, in △ABE, 𝑙(AB)2=𝑙(AE)2+𝑙(BE)2=(35)2+(12)2=1225+144\begin{matrix} \mathit{l}(AB)^{2} & \mathit{\ } = \mathit{l}(AE)^{2} + \mathit{l}(BE)^{2} \\ & \mathit{\ } = (35)^{2} + (12)^{2} = 1225 + 144 \end{matrix} ∴𝑙(𝐴𝐵)2=1369
∴𝑙(𝐴𝐵)=37
In △𝐸𝐵𝐶,𝑙(𝐵𝐶)2=𝑙(𝐸𝐶)2−𝑙(𝐵𝐸)2 =(15)2−(12)2=225−144 ∴𝑙(𝐵𝐶)2=81∴𝑙(𝐵𝐶)=9
In △ECD,𝑙(CD)2=𝑙(ED)2−𝑙(EC)2 =(17)2−(15)2=289−225 ∴𝑙(𝐶𝐷)2=64∴𝑙(𝐶𝐷)=8
Perimeter of pentagon ABCDE=AB+BC+CD+ED+AE =37+9+8+17+35=106 units. \begin{matrix} & \mathit{\ } = 37 + 9 + 8 + 17 + 35 \\ & \mathit{\ } = 106\text{~units.~} \end{matrix} ∴ the correct answer is option (2).

questions.text: The area of a circular garden is 5,54,400 m2. The circumference of the garden will be = ?
questions.solution:
a) Area of a circular garden =554400 m2
The area of a circular garden =𝜋𝑟2 ∴554400=227×12∴554400×722=𝑟2∴25200×7=𝑟2,∴𝑟2=25200×7=100×252×7∴𝑟2=100×36×7×7∴𝑟=100×36×7×7=10×10×6×6×7×7∴𝑟=10×6×7=420 m\begin{matrix} & \mathit{\ }\therefore 554400 = \frac{22}{7} \times 1^{2}\ \therefore\frac{554400 \times 7}{22} = \mathit{r}^{2} \\ & \mathit{\ }\therefore 25200 \times 7 = \mathit{r}^{2},\therefore\mathit{r}^{2} = 25200 \times 7 = 100 \times 252 \times 7 \\ & \mathit{\ }\therefore\mathit{r}^{2} = 100 \times 36 \times 7 \times 7 \\ & \mathit{\ }\therefore\mathit{r} = \sqrt{100 \times 36 \times 7 \times 7} \\ & \ = \sqrt{10 \times 10 \times 6 \times 6 \times 7 \times 7} \\ & \mathit{\ }\therefore\mathit{r} = 10 \times 6 \times 7 = 420\text{ }m \end{matrix} The circumference of the circular garden =2𝜋𝑟 =2×227×420 Circumference of the garden =2640 m.
∴ the correct answer is option (1).

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The length, breadth and height of a cuboidal shape tin box is 120 cm,80 cm and 150 cm respectively. The box is to be coloured from insides as well as from outside. (The top of the box can be opened). What will be the expenses to colour the box at the rate of 175 per m2 ? (Assuming the thickness is negligible.)
questions.solution:
b) 𝑙=120 cm=120100 m=1.2 m,𝑏=80 cm=0.8 m,ℎ=150 cm=1.5 m.
Inner surface area of the box = Outer surface area of the box.
Inner surface area of the box =2(𝑙𝑏+𝑏ℎ+𝑙ℎ) =2(1.2×0.8+0.8×1.5+1.2×1.5)=2(0.96+1.20+1.8)=2×3.96\begin{matrix} & \mathit{\ } = 2(1.2 \times 0.8 + 0.8 \times 1.5 + 1.2 \times 1.5) \\ & \mathit{\ } = 2(0.96 + 1.20 + 1.8) \\ & \mathit{\ } = 2 \times 3.96 \end{matrix} ∴ inner surface area of box =7.92 m2.
∴ outer surface area of the box =7.92 m2.
Total surface area for colour =7.92+7.92=15.84 m2.
Expenses for colouring the box = Rate per m2× Surface area =₹175×15.84=₹2772.  ∴ the correct answer is option (2).

questions.subject: Paper - 2 (SAT)
questions.text: The measure of major arc of a circle is 60∘ less than 3 times the measure of the corresponding minor arc. What is the measure of the major arc of the circle?
questions.solution:
a) Let the measure of the minor arc be 𝑥∘.
From the given condition, measure of corresponding major arc will be (3𝑥−60)∘.
∴𝑥+(3𝑥−60)=360
... (Measure of complete arc of circle)
∴𝑥+3𝑥−60=360
∴4𝑥=360+60∴4𝑥=420∴𝑥=105∘
The measure of the minor arc=105∘.
The measure of corresponding major arc =360∘−105∘=255∘
∴ the correct answer is option (1).
